title: Removing the trading panels (decided 23 Sep) will silently discard an upgrading user's portfolio, watchlist, notes and research memory whenever their last autosave had a broker panel docked
repro: Scratch vitest ($ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/vt/upgrade.test.ts): register every first-party module EXCEPT broker-connect (the post-trading-removal build), stub the autosave GET to return the operator's real historical blob __autosave__.vysted-workspace.bak-r7-sweep (layout holds broker-connect + broker-order-entry beside a portfolio with holdings, a 7-name watchlist, notes, a research space) -> restoreLastSessionOrDefault returns false, api.fromJSON called 0 times, default layout applied (addPanel 1), deserializeWorkspace never runs, so no non-layout slice is applied; the page/PanelHost autosave subscriptions then overwrite __autosave__ with default stores. Control: the live 19-Sep blob (chart/brief/portfolio only) restores fine (restored=true).
evidence: $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/workspace-upgrade-vitest.txt (GATE lines); src/lib/workspace.ts:512-515 (unknown-component skip returns before deserializeWorkspace), src/lib/workspace.ts:265 (layout restored before every other slice); src/components/PanelHost.tsx:188-193 + src/app/page.tsx:108-181 (autosave persists the defaults); src/modules/broker-connect/index.ts:51 (the panel ids that will disappear); census COD-workspace-layout-4 (same mechanism, filed hypothetically)
notes: The subject is the user's own tracked portfolio, watchlist and notes, not the broker feature, so it stays in scope even though the trigger is the trading removal. This turns COD-workspace-layout-4's 'one component-id rename in a release' into a scheduled, reproduced event on a real historical blob. It becomes critical data loss the moment the removal ships without a guard, because holdings live ONLY in the workspace blob (portfolios.list[].holdings) and portfolio.db is a separate store. Smallest fix, as part of the trading-removal change: strip unknown panel ids from the serialized layout (or map broker-* to nothing) BEFORE the unknown-component gate, and restore the non-layout slices regardless of the layout outcome (COD-workspace-layout-4's fix). Add a regression test that feeds bak-r7-sweep's shape through a build without broker-connect.

title: No persistent store records a schema version: user_version is 0 on all 8 SQLite DBs and the workspace blob has no top-level version, so upgrade safety rests on 3 ad-hoc additive column guards
repro: Copy the 19-Sep 0.8.0 data dir (sqlite .backup), boot current source on it, then `sqlite3 <db> 'PRAGMA user_version'` for audit_log, custom_agents, data_cache, delegate_runs, fundamentals_cache, plugins, portfolio, workflows -> 0 for every one, before and after boot. It reads clean today only because 0.8.0 -> HEAD changed no schema (git log since 19 Sep: d328089, 0c63d46, 0112a0c, none store-touching).
evidence: $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/pre-boot-schema.txt + post-boot-schema.txt; additive guards only at sidecar/services/fundamentals_store.py:172-182, sidecar/services/runs_store.py:94-102, sidecar/services/plugins_store.py:53-67; CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS-only at sidecar/services/portfolio_db.py:26-35, agents_store.py:23 ('no schema migrations'), workflow_store.py:26-34, data_cache.py:59-65, models/audit_log.py:21; blob versioning only for one field: src/lib/workspace.ts:174 (MODEL_OVERRIDES_VERSION); retired cache namespace never cleaned: 2,678 screener:* rows orphaned since 5142aa1 (12 Jun)
notes: Each store re-invents migration by hand, and only for 'add a nullable/defaulted column'. A rename, a type change, a NOT NULL column without a default, a key-namespace retirement (already happened: screener:* in data_cache) or a blob-field reshape has no mechanism. Nothing backs up the data dir before a new build first touches it, and no build can detect that a NEWER build wrote the dir (downgrade). Consequence: the first non-additive change in 1.x is either a crash on every existing install (the failure class the fundamentals _migrate finding already flagged) or a silent drop. Smallest fix: one shared sidecar helper, e.g. `migrate(conn, steps: list[str])` keyed on PRAGMA user_version and used by all 8 stores; a top-level `schemaVersion` on SerializedWorkspace with a migrate chain in deserializeWorkspace; and a one-time copy of the data dir to `backups/<old-version>/` when the stored app version differs from the running one.

title: A v0.8.0-tag user's tracked portfolio does not survive the upgrade: holdings stay in portfolio.db, but the current panel never reads it and shows 'This portfolio is empty'
repro: git archive v0.8.0 sidecar -> run the TAG's own portfolio_db.create_position x3 (RELIANCE.NS x10 @2890.55, TCS.NS x5, BTC/USDT x0.05, notes) into an empty data dir ($ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/seed_v080.py) -> boot CURRENT source on it (:52228) -> GET /portfolio/positions 200 returns all 3 rows -> scratch vitest (vt/v080tag.test.tsx) drives the current frontend against that sidecar: restoreLastSessionOrDefault (no __autosave__, as at the tag) -> portfolios store 'Portfolio:0'; mount PortfolioPanel -> 'This portfolio is empty ... Add your first holding'; loadWorkspace('my-desk') (a tag-shape named workspace) -> still 'Portfolio:0'. The frontend made 2 fetches (GET /workspace/__autosave__, GET /workspace/my-desk) and 0 to /portfolio/positions.
evidence: $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/v080tag-frontend-vitest.txt, $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/v080tag-reads.txt; git show v0.8.0:src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:55 + git show v0.8.0:src/modules/portfolio/api.ts:15,46,51,56 (the tag's portfolio was the sidecar SQLite store); commit 12862d3 (1 Jun, 'Drops the dead sidecar CRUD', no data step); src/lib/workspace.ts:286-289 ('older blobs lack them - keep the empty default'); src/store/portfolios.ts:112-114 (empty seed); src/modules/portfolio/api.ts:4-5 ('there is NO sidecar positions CRUD'); src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:817 (empty state); src/lib/host-actions.ts:1254-1259,1321-1340 (only caller: agent write-sync into the same table)
notes: The tracked portfolio is in scope (manual holdings, not trading). Nothing is deleted, but from the user's side it is lost: no notice, no import, no surface that reads the old rows. The agent's portfolio_add_position then POSTs new rows beside the orphaned ones, so the dead ledger silently mixes pre- and post-upgrade holdings (COD-portfolio-2/-3 cover the fork itself; this finding is the upgrade consequence, measured). v0.8.0 is a pushed tag with no binary release (gh release list empty), and the operator's own portfolio.db has 0 rows, so the affected population today is tag builders. It becomes critical (data loss) for any 0.8.0 build that was distributed. Smallest fix: a one-time import on restore. When the blob has no `portfolios` key and GET /portfolio/positions is non-empty, seed the default portfolio from those rows (symbol/quantity/cost_basis/asset_class/note), mark the import in the blob, then retire the SQLite ledger per COD-portfolio-3.

title: A custom agent saved on the v0.8.0 tag silently loses its 'macro' tool: the id was renamed on 31 May with no alias or row migration, and every adapter drops unknown ids without a log or event
repro: The tag's agents_store.create_agent(custom:macro-hawk, tools=['price_data','macro','news']) (all valid at v0.8.0) -> boot current source -> GET /custom-agents returns tools ['price_data','macro','news'] unchanged -> in-process schemas.openai_tools/anthropic_tools(spec.tools) -> ['price_data','news'] ('macro' in TOOL_SCHEMAS: False) -> PUT /custom-agents/custom:macro-hawk with the same tools -> 422 "unknown tool ids: ['macro']". The agent's system prompt still says 'Always check the macro series first'.
evidence: $ISO/seat-l4-upgrade/evidence/v080tag-agent-tools.txt; git show v0.8.0:sidecar/models/custom_agent.py:30-38 (tag allow-list includes 'macro'); commit 0e248f9 (31 May, allow-list re-derived from the catalog; ids now macro_series/macro_search); sidecar/services/agent_tools/schemas.py:50-51 (_known() filters silently); sidecar/models/custom_agent.py:55-63 (PUT rejects); src/modules/agent-builder/form.tsx:139-141 (the builder strips ids outside its 20-entry list, which lacks both 'macro' and 'news'); sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:94-96 (an 'aliases' field exists; `grep -rn '\.aliases' sidecar` has no reader)
notes: Distinct from COD-frontend-panels-agent-shell-2, which covers the builder's client-side strip. Here the server itself renamed a persisted id with no mapping, so an untouched agent degrades at invoke time with no signal to the user or in the log. A model told to check macro first, with no macro tool, is set up to answer without macro data. The same thing recurs on every future catalog rename, because persisted tool ids have no version and no alias resolution. Smallest fix: resolve persisted ids through Capability.aliases (add 'macro' to macro_series) in the custom-agent validator and in _known(), and make _known() log plus emit a one-time 'tool X is no longer available' notice for anything still unresolved.
